description:
Search and filter the user's expenses. Returns matching expense rows from their spreadsheet. Filter by category, merchant, date range, amount, or tags. Results are paginated: when hasMore is true, call again with nextCursor and the same filters. Do not split a date range into repeated overlapping searches.

Use the optional query parameter for deterministic natural-language recall over merchant, city/location, Notes (including receipt items, delivery source, payer, and Business purpose), Tag, and category. Each matching result includes matchedFields and a short matchReason so you can explain why it was selected. When several rows plausibly match, a disambiguation list is returned; each option carries the exact expenseId. Structured filters (categories, merchants, dateRange, tags, minAmount, maxAmount) combine with the query using AND semantics. Each result includes expenseId, the exact durable Receipt ID required by update_expense. For country-based grouping or client-assignment review, use groupBy:country with explicit YYYY-MM-DD start/end. This read-only mode reviews at most 100 matching master expenses; narrow the range if too large. Use exact configured categories for travel, not an assumption that every foreign expense is travel. Unknown locations remain separate; currency never establishes country. Country review supports categories, merchants, tags, countries and tagAssignment, not free query or pagination. Show counts and currency-separated totals, then use exact returned IDs/current tags in group_expenses after the user chooses destinations.

clientEmail.description: Client account email. Accountants may use this only for an accepted ExpenseBot client.

countries.description: Country-review filter: supported country names/codes, or unknown. Never infer a country from currency or an ambiguous city.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor returned by the previous search_expenses page. Reuse the same filters; never construct or edit this value.

dateRange.description: Time period filter. Use exactly one variant — pick the shape that matches the user's phrasing.

value.description: Relative range phrase, e.g., 'last month', 'YTD', 'this quarter', 'last 7 days'

groupBy.description: Read-only country review; requires explicit dateRange.start/end and at most 100 matches.

hasReceipt.description: When true, return only expenses with a receipt link. When false, return only expenses without one.

query.description: Optional natural-language recall over the user's existing expense fields (merchant, city/location, Notes including receipt items, delivery source, payer, and Business purpose, Tag, category). Deterministic case-insensitive matching — no embeddings or model classifiers. Combine with structured filters using AND semantics. Examples: 'Tribeca restaurant', 'Bodewell project hardware store', 'client dinner note'.

tagAssignment.description: Country review: unassigned means blank/Business; no_client means no canonical client tag, including project/trip-tagged rows. Neither implies business use.

name: search_expenses

countryGroups.description: Complete bounded country review; unknown locations remain separate.

expenses.description: Matching expense rows, newest first, paginated.

amount.description: Amount in currency; country review uses original receipt currency.

expenseId.description: Durable Receipt ID (Column Q). The only identity accepted by update_expense.

nextCursor.description: Opaque signed continuation; reuse with identical filters.

total.description: Home-currency sum in normal search; null in country review. Use countryGroups totalsByCurrency, never sum currencies.
